title: Deeper and broader FreeCAD DXF transform and malformed-input acceptance review
mode: primary-source web research and read-only local plan reconciliation
scope: Recheck the current status and final diagnosis of a recent FreeCAD DXF block-transform report
Ground INSERT scale-factor test vectors in Autodesk DXF/ObjectARX documentation
Refine valid-file versus malformed-file acceptance in the existing FreeCAD consumer gate
Preserve the current implementation queue and fast per-slice validation cadence

method.kind: Read current primary project issue/documentation and reconcile the existing plan
method.limitations: The FreeCAD issue attachment was not downloaded or inspected. Issue comments are reporter/maintainer statements, not an independent reproduction. Autodesk API pages document individual scale properties but do not alone establish every version-specific nested transform composition. No current FreeCAD importer or converter was executed.

sources.revision: Issue state and activity reviewed 2026-10-18; opened 2026-03-31 and closed by the reporter 2026-04-21
sources.observed: The initial report described mirrored blocks in a Windows FreeCAD development build, with another user confirming on the same build. The reporter later said the supplied DXF was corrupted and closed the issue. The report lacks a minimized malformed tag and normative recovery expectation. It is not a confirmed FreeCAD or libdxfrw transform defect and is not a valid-DXF conformance oracle.

X/Y/Z block-reference scale factors correspond to DXF group codes 41/42/43 and are applied relative to perceived WCS axes. The native setter rejects zero scale factors. These pages do not by themselves establish all nested INSERT, block-base, rotation, extrusion/OCS, unit, and version interactions.

sources.project: FreeCAD importer and DWG conversion documentation
sources.observed: The docs distinguish C++ and legacy Python DXF import paths and describe a converter-followed-by-DXF-import DWG route. They are a route description only, not a qualification of a current application binary, platform, preference, or converter.

assessment.planImpact: Refines the existing PAR-07/S8 composed FreeCAD consumer gate with locally authored asymmetric/nested INSERT transform controls and independently computed expected geometry. Valid DXF compatibility and malformed-input recovery are separate outcomes. Exact importer backend, converter, platform, version, diagnostics, object disposition, transformed coordinates/bounds, orientation, and units are recorded. No change to local implementation ordering or per-slice cost.

implementationReadyChecks: At the existing composed consumer checkpoint, use a valid locally authored DXF with asymmetric geometry, nonzero block base, nested INSERTs, translation, rotation, nonuniform scale, and only profile-valid reflection/OCS cases.
Calculate transformed sample points and expected bounds independently from the importer; report orientation/handedness and unit conversion explicitly.
Validate converter output with the strict local reader and bind its hash and effective version before invoking FreeCAD.
Run C++ and legacy importer backends separately when each is in the support scope; capture exact FreeCAD build, platform, settings, object inventory, losses, and diagnostics.

If malformed recovery is studied, use a minimized mutation of a locally generated control and report only recovery/disposition; do not grade it as valid-file compatibility or assume cross-application recovery equivalence.
Do not use FreeCAD 2D import results to qualify ACIS/AcDs association, B-rep validity, or native 3D support.
Do not download or commit third-party/customer drawings; preserve the fast local-slice validation cadence and scheduled/composed external checks.
